financials_interim.notes: COMPANY (standalone) basis. EPS 2.02 = 599,658k/297,123,750 confirmed. See GROUP row's notes for shared extraction/verification detail.

Haycarb PLC (Hayleys Group, activated carbon / environmental engineering manufacturer with multiple overseas subsidiaries in Thailand, Indonesia, UK, Australia, USA, Philippines, Singapore, Germany, India). Clean single-rendering filing, no dual-extraction ambiguity. The Group adopted SLFRS 18 (new P&L presentation standard) effective 1 April 2025 -- 'Foreign exchange differences' is now presented as a genuine line ABOVE operating_profit (not a below-the-line financing item), and the filing's own Note 3 reconciles the prior-year comparative from the old LKAS 1 presentation to confirm this reclassification does not change PBT/PAT. operating_profit = the filing's own 'Operating profit' subtotal (2,278,057 Group / 1,288,925 Company), which already includes the FX-differences line. finance_costs = 'Interest expenses on loans and borrowings' (368,520 Group / 218,227 Company) + 'Foreign exchange differences on interest-bearing loans and borrowings' (364,883 Group / 354,367 Company) = 733,403 Group / 572,594 Company -- both genuine financing-related costs per the filing's own structure between Operating result before financing/tax and PBT. EPS cross-check: Group 1,099,009k/297,123,750 shares=3.699~=3.70 disclosed; Company 599,658k/297,123,750=2.018~=2.02 disclosed -- both tie exactly, no column-swap issues. short_term_borrowings = current 'Interest-bearing loans and borrowings' (includes bank overdrafts per the cash-flow note's 'Bank overdrafts and short-term loans' analysis); long_term_borrowings = non-current 'Interest-bearing loans and borrowings'. capex = 'Purchase of property, plant and equipment' + 'Acquisition of intangible assets'.

interim_updates.note_text: Haycarb's Group revenue grew 44.7% YoY to Rs.19.80bn for Q1 FY2026/27 (three months ended 30 June 2026), with gross profit up 46.6% to Rs.3.91bn (margin roughly flat at 19.8% vs 19.5%). This is genuine, broad-based operating growth, not primarily an FX effect: gross profit alone rose Rs.1.24bn, which exceeds the entire Rs.1.17bn increase in operating profit (Rs.1.11bn to Rs.2.28bn) even after administrative expenses grew 27.6% (Rs.1.64bn to Rs.2.10bn). By segment, Activated Carbon (the core business, ~91% of segment PBT) drove the improvement: segment PBT +68.6% YoY (Rs.988.8mn to Rs.1,667.3mn), while the smaller Environmental Engineering segment's loss widened (-Rs.20.3mn to -Rs.38.0mn). Below operating profit, however, financing costs rose sharply: Interest expenses on loans and borrowings +147.4% (Rs.149.0mn to Rs.368.5mn) and, more strikingly, Foreign exchange differences on interest-bearing loans and borrowings swung from a Rs.19.5mn loss to a Rs.364.9mn loss -- together these financing costs (Rs.733.4mn combined, from Rs.168.5mn) consumed roughly 63% of the operating-profit gain, which is why PBT grew a slower 68.2% (Rs.973.2mn to Rs.1,637.0mn) despite operating profit more than doubling. PAT still grew a strong 83.1% (Rs.676.5mn to Rs.1,238.7mn) as the tax charge grew more slowly (+34.2%) than PBT. The standalone Company grew even faster than the Group (PAT +70.7% to Rs.599.7mn), and declared a first interim dividend of Rs.0.75/share (2025/26: Rs.0.50/share).
interim_updates.gaps_note: No QoQ comparison possible: no quarter closer to this one has been collected for HAYC -- this is the first financial_statements entry for this symbol. Local document archive had also skipped the 31 December 2025 and 31 March 2026 (year-end) interim filings -- per this project's established convention of entering only the newly-flagged period (not backfilling every gap), only this newest quarter (30 June 2026) was sourced and entered; the intervening gaps were not backfilled.
interim_updates.takeaway: This is a genuinely strong operating quarter -- gross profit growth alone exceeds the total increase in operating profit, and it's concentrated in the core Activated Carbon segment (+69% PBT), not a one-off. The one real caveat is financing cost: interest expense on borrowings rose 147% and FX losses on interest-bearing debt swung sharply negative (likely reflecting LKR movements against the currencies of Haycarb's overseas subsidiary borrowings), together absorbing about two-thirds of the operating-profit gain before it reached PBT -- worth monitoring if debt costs or currency volatility persist.
operational_highlights: Group revenue +44.7% YoY to Rs.19.80bn; gross profit +46.6% to Rs.3.91bn (margin roughly flat at 19.8%)
Operating profit more than doubled YoY (Rs.1.11bn to Rs.2.28bn), driven by the Activated Carbon segment, whose PBT rose 68.6% to Rs.1,667.3mn (~91% of total segment PBT)
Environmental Engineering segment's loss widened from Rs.20.3mn to Rs.38.0mn -- the one segment moving the wrong way

Interest expenses on loans and borrowings +147.4% YoY (Rs.149.0mn to Rs.368.5mn); FX differences on interest-bearing borrowings swung from a Rs.19.5mn loss to a Rs.364.9mn loss -- together these financing costs absorbed roughly 63% of the operating-profit gain
Group PBT +68.2% YoY to Rs.1,637.0mn; PAT +83.1% to Rs.1,238.7mn as the tax charge grew more slowly (+34.2%) than PBT
First interim dividend of Rs.0.75/share declared (2025/26: Rs.0.50/share); standalone Company PAT grew even faster than Group (+70.7% to Rs.599.7mn)
key_drivers: Activated Carbon segment PBT +68.6% YoY (Rs.988.8mn to Rs.1,667.3mn) is the primary driver of both revenue and profit growth -- a genuine, core-business improvement, not an FX or one-off item

Foreign exchange differences on interest-bearing loans and borrowings swung from a Rs.19.5mn loss to a Rs.364.9mn loss, the single largest drag between operating profit and PBT -- likely reflects LKR movements against the currencies of overseas subsidiary debt (Thailand, Indonesia, UK, Australia, USA and other subsidiaries)

Interest expenses on loans and borrowings nearly two-and-a-half times higher YoY (+147.4%), consistent with a larger current-borrowings balance (Rs.17.09bn at 30 June 2026 vs Rs.14.69bn at 31 March 2026)
